description: NIST's FTC-11, its AP242 edition 2's solid #1299 alone (excerpted with tools/oracle/excerpt.py): the convex edge between the plane f0 and the cylinder f39, written as a cubic B-spline of one span that hides a circle (r 0.2151, within 9.7e-5 of the faces' own section, the edge's tolerance 2.5e-3), filleted alone at the battery's radius. Its chain runs on at both tangent vertices: along the line e1 to v2, a convex kink of 7.3° where the plane f38 stands 2.3e-3 off tangent to the boss f37, its end arc across f37 at a grazing angle, inside the band the file's pcurves of f37's rim stand off its curve by (3.75e-3, the rim's tolerance); and along the line e19 to v19, a step whose corner edge e18 is lengthened to the trim. Arris builds it as Open CASCADE does, within its volume, area and centroid (plans/nurbs-face-blend step 10b); the checker at Full decides every pair (steps 10c and 10d). Open CASCADE reading Arris's STEP finds the plane f0 larger by 1.19e-2 than in its own blend (area 2.2e-6 relative, volume 6.4e-8), and the whole of that is the one B-spline edge of the boss's rim on f0: Open CASCADE's own wire is open there, the edge ending 2.0e-3 from the next edge's start, Arris' 2.4e-4 (both within the vertex's tolerance 3.7e-3), and the area of an open wire in a plane's frame depends on the gap and on its distance from the frame's origin, here 51 away: 0.5 x 51 x 2.0e-3 is 5e-2 for a gap, 1e-2 for the part of it the two wires differ by. Every other edge of f0 agrees to 1e-6 in its contribution to the area and the circles to 5e-5 in 1414. So the measure tolerances are widened to the oracle's own uncertainty (volume 2e-7, area 5e-6, centroid 5e-6, inertia 3e-7), still three orders under what a wrong radius, junction or end moves (ADR-0062's step 10e amendment)

analytic.counts_differ: Open CASCADE keeps the consumed corner vertex v19 on the lengthened corner edge e18, two edges of one line between the same two faces; Arris lengthens the one edge to the trim (ADR-0038)
